name: aob_find
title: Find byte patterns
description: Find up to 8 array-of-bytes patterns (hex bytes and ?? wildcards) and report each pattern's matches, whether the count is exact and whether it is unique. The patterns are scanned one after another in one Cheat Engine call that blocks Cheat Engine until the last scan ends: without module or startAddress/endAddress each pattern scans the whole target, so scope the call, and use executable=required for code. Uniqueness needs limit 2 or more. Mapped memory, such as emulator RAM, is skipped unless Cheat Engine's scan settings include it or includeMapped is true.

patterns.description: The patterns, 1 to 8, each up to 4096 byte positions, such as 48 8B ?? ?? ?? ?? 89 43 10.

module.description: Scan only this loaded module's image, such as game.exe; faster and cannot match in another module.

startAddress.description: The first allowed match address or expression; requires endAddress.

endAddress.description: The last allowed match address or expression; requires startAddress.

writable.description: Whether matches must be in writable memory: required, excluded or any (default).

executable.description: Whether matches must be in executable memory: required, excluded or any (default).

copyOnWrite.description: Whether matches must be in copy-on-write memory: required, excluded or any (default).

alignment.description: Only match addresses divisible by this number, such as 4; not with lastDigits.

lastDigits.description: Only match addresses whose hexadecimal form ends with these 1 to 16 digits; not with alignment.

limit.description: The most matches to list per pattern, 1 to 10000.

includeMapped.description: Whether this call also scans mapped memory (MEM_MAPPED: file views and shared sections, such as an emulator's guest RAM), which Cheat Engine skips unless its scan settings include it. Cheat Engine's MEM_MAPPED override is Cheat Engine-wide: this scan turns it on and then ends every scan-region override (setSpecialScanOptionsOverride), including one that a table or lua_execute set. Scans that run in parallel with it must use the same includeMapped, or are refused as busy. Not with module, whose image is never mapped memory.

results.description: One entry per requested pattern, in request order.

pattern.description: The pattern as scanned: uppercase byte pairs and ?? wildcards separated by single spaces.

exact.description: Whether count is proven to be every match in scope; false when the limit cut the list or Cheat Engine cannot tell zero matches from a failure.

unique.description: Whether exactly one match exists in scope: exact and count 1. Use a limit of at least 2.

scope.description: What Cheat Engine scanned: bounded_scan (only the module or range), global_scan, filtered_global_scan (whole target, then filtered) or unknown.

targetVerified.description: Whether the matches belong to one confirmed target incarnation for the whole scan.

elapsedMs.description: How long Cheat Engine's scan and the copy of its result took, in milliseconds.

matches.description: The match addresses in Cheat Engine's order, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

name: aob_find_value
title: Find value bytes
description: Encode one typed value as the little-endian bytes the target would hold (integers in two's complement, float and double by their exact bits, a pointer at the target's pointer size, string as UTF-8 and wstring as UTF-16 without a terminator) and find those bytes with one array-of-bytes scan, without creating scanner state. Returns the pattern used and its matches. Only exact bit patterns match: for a rounded or approximate value use scan_first, and for raw bytes or wildcards use aob_find. The scan blocks Cheat Engine while it runs: without module or startAddress/endAddress it scans the whole target, so scope it. alignment defaults to the value's size up to 4 for numbers and pointers; 1-byte integers and strings match at any address. Mapped memory is skipped unless Cheat Engine's scan settings include it or includeMapped is true. Uniqueness needs limit 2 or more.

value.description: The value as text: decimal or 0x hexadecimal integers, invariant floats (NaN, Infinity), a hexadecimal pointer or the text of a string, at most 4096 encoded bytes.

module.description: Scan only this loaded module's image, such as game.exe; faster and cannot match in another module.

startAddress.description: The first allowed match address or expression; requires endAddress.

endAddress.description: The last allowed match address or expression; requires startAddress.

writable.description: Whether matches must be in writable memory: required, excluded or any (default).

executable.description: Whether matches must be in executable memory: required, excluded or any (default).

copyOnWrite.description: Whether matches must be in copy-on-write memory: required, excluded or any (default).

alignment.description: Only match addresses divisible by this number, 1 to 65536; defaults to the value's size up to 4 for numbers and pointers, and to no alignment filter (any address) for 1-byte integers and strings.

limit.description: The most matches to list, 1 to 10000.

includeMapped.description: Whether this call also scans mapped memory (MEM_MAPPED: file views and shared sections, such as an emulator's guest RAM), which Cheat Engine skips unless its scan settings include it. Cheat Engine's MEM_MAPPED override is Cheat Engine-wide: this scan turns it on and then ends every scan-region override (setSpecialScanOptionsOverride), including one that a table or lua_execute set. Scans that run in parallel with it must use the same includeMapped, or are refused as busy. Not with module, whose image is never mapped memory.

value.description: The value text as given.

result.description: The scan: pattern holds the encoded little-endian bytes as scanned, then the matches as aob_find reports them.

exact.description: Whether count is proven to be every match in scope; false when the limit cut the list or Cheat Engine cannot tell zero matches from a failure.

unique.description: Whether exactly one match exists in scope: exact and count 1. Use a limit of at least 2.

scope.description: What Cheat Engine scanned: bounded_scan (only the module or range), global_scan, filtered_global_scan (whole target, then filtered) or unknown.

targetVerified.description: Whether the matches belong to one confirmed target incarnation for the whole scan.

elapsedMs.description: How long Cheat Engine's scan and the copy of its result took, in milliseconds.

name: aob_generate_signature
title: Generate an AOB signature
description: Generate an array-of-bytes signature that finds an address inside a loaded module and prove it with bounded scans of that module; generator says which ran. In a module of at most 64 MiB, Cheat Engine's getUniqueAOB builds it from up to 20 bytes on each side of the address (see offset), then a separate scan verifies it. In a larger module, where getUniqueAOB would list and read every match of the instruction bytes, a managed generator starts at the address and adds whole instructions, wildcarding RIP-relative, absolute and branch displacements and 4- or 8-byte values of at least 0x10000, until a module scan finds it once, for at most 64 bytes and 6 scans. Blocks Cheat Engine while it scans; review the pattern before relying on it.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression inside a loaded module, such as game.exe+1C0.

module.description: The module that must contain the address; defaults to the module that contains it.

verify.description: Whether to verify Cheat Engine's signature with a separate bounded scan of the module; a managed signature is always verified, because its scans build it.

address.description: The resolved address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

module.description: The module that contains the address and was scanned.

generator.description: Which generator ran: cheat_engine (Cheat Engine's getUniqueAOB, for a module of at most 64 MiB) or managed (whole instructions decoded forward from the address and extended until a module scan proves the pattern unique, for a larger module).

unique.description: Whether the signature matches only once in the module: proven by a bounded module scan when verified is true.

verified.description: Whether a bounded scan of the module checked the signature; always true for a managed signature, whose scans build it, and false when verify is false or no signature was generated.

pattern.description: The signature, uppercase byte pairs and ?? wildcards; omitted when no signature was generated.

patternStart.description: Where a match of the signature begins, uppercase hexadecimal: the address minus offset.

offset.description: The distance in bytes from patternStart to the address; inject at match+offset. Always 0 for a managed signature, which starts at the address.

matchCount.description: How many matches the verification scan found; 2 means at least 2. Omitted when not verified.

triedPattern.description: The last pattern tried when no signature was generated (unique is false and pattern is omitted), which matches more than once: the instruction bytes at the address that Cheat Engine reported, or the managed generator's longest pattern, at most 64 bytes.

name: asm_check
title: Check Auto Assembler
description: Check an Auto Assembler script without applying it: Cheat Engine checks ENABLE, then DISABLE if ENABLE passed; failedSection names the rejected section. Cheat Engine runs parts of a script while checking it, so the server refuses, as unsupported, any script that needs a switch beyond auto_assembler (such as {$lua}, {$c}, luacall, loadlibrary, include or a Lua-registered command like USEMONO), uses globalalloc, which allocates memory even during a check, or writes $ before anything but hexadecimal digits, which Cheat Engine evaluates as Lua; review it by reading it. Commands in // and /* */ comments are ignored, as Cheat Engine removes those first. Its symbol handler still resolves addresses and operands, consulting symbol-lookup callbacks that Lua registered, such as the shipped luasymbols.lua, which reads an unknown name as Lua. DISABLE is checked without ENABLE's symbols, so symbol+4 there is rejected although a release would resolve it. Success proves no later apply or release.

script.description: A complete Auto Assembler source with ENABLE and DISABLE sections, up to 1048576 characters and 1048576 UTF-8 bytes.

name.description: An optional diagnostic patch name, up to 256 characters.

accepted.description: Whether Cheat Engine accepted both the ENABLE and the DISABLE section. A true result does not apply the patch.

hostMessages.description: Cheat Engine's bounded, unparsed diagnostic text for the rejected section, when it returned any.

hostMessagesTruncated.description: Whether hostMessages was truncated to its bound.

failedSection.description: The section Cheat Engine rejected, enable or disable; omitted when accepted is true.

name: asm_generate_api_hook
title: Generate API hook
description: Ask Cheat Engine's generateAPIHookScript for an Auto Assembler hook that sends execution at address to jumpTarget, without applying it. The script's ENABLE section allocates originalcall, which holds the instructions the jump overwrites followed by a jump back, adds a jump trampoline on x64, and writes the jump at address; its DISABLE section restores the original bytes and frees what ENABLE allocated. Review the generated source and run asm_check before an explicit asm_apply.

address.description: The address or expression of the function or instruction to hook; Cheat Engine overwrites the whole instructions that the jump covers.

jumpTarget.description: The address or expression of the replacement code that the hook jumps to.

newCallAddress.description: An optional address or symbol where the ENABLE section stores the address of originalcall (dq on x64, dd on x86), so the replacement code can call the original instructions; DISABLE does not restore it. Up to 256 characters.

extension.description: An optional suffix Cheat Engine appends to the script's label and allocation names (originalcall, returnhere, jumptrampoline), so two generated hooks can share one script: up to 64 ASCII letters, digits or underscores.

targetSelf.description: Whether Cheat Engine should generate a hook in its own process.

script.description: The generated Auto Assembler source. Review, check and explicitly apply it separately.

expectedBytes.description: The validated original bytes asserted before an injection writes its jump; empty when Cheat Engine generated an API-hook script.

symbolName.description: The symbol the script registers while enabled, when generated as an injection.

name: asm_generate_injection

It asserts the original bytes, allocates only while enabled, restores the bytes and releases its allocation and symbol while disabled. signature must be a verified unique module signature from aob_generate_signature; pass its offset too, so the scaffold injects at the match start plus offset, where symbolName is registered. Review the template, then use asm_check before any apply.

name: code_get_function_graph

title: Start code dissect

name: exec_call_local
title: Call Cheat Engine function
description: Call a one-parameter stdcall function in Cheat Engine's own process. localAddress is resolved in Cheat Engine, rather than the selected target. Cheat Engine provides no timeout for this API, so call only a routine known to return promptly; a refusal after admission has hostEffect unknown.

localAddress.description: Cheat Engine local address or expression of the function.

parameter.description: Integer or pointer passed to the function as its exact 64-bit value (10 passes 10); a negative value passes its two's-complement bits.

functionAddress.description: The called function address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

returnValue.description: The function's integer return register (EAX or RAX) as Cheat Engine reported it, as decimal text.

name: exec_call_method
title: Call target instance method
description: Call an instance method in the selected target with up to 16 numeric typed arguments, whose values are JSON strings even for integers. Allocate and write text or buffers with memory_allocate and memory_write, then pass the allocation address as an integer so it remains alive after a timeout. functionAddress and classInstance are resolved through Client before the call. classRegister, 1 (ECX/RCX) by default, carries this. On a 32-bit target the arguments go on the stack. On a 64-bit target, classRegister 1 makes the Microsoft x64 member call: this in RCX, then argument 1 in RDX or XMM1, 2 in R8 or XMM2, 3 in R9 or XMM3 and the rest on the stack. With another register the arguments start at RCX or XMM0, as in exec_call_remote, and a register that an argument would overwrite is refused. Calls refuse a paused or debugger-stopped target and wait at most 10 seconds; inspect the target before retrying an unknown result.

functionAddress.description: Address or Cheat Engine expression of the instance method.

classInstance.description: Address or Cheat Engine expression of the object instance.

classRegister.description: Register that carries this: 0 EAX/RAX, 1 ECX/RCX, 2 EDX/RDX, 3 EBX/RBX, 5 EBP/RBP, 6 ESI/RSI, 7 EDI/RDI, 8 to 15 R8 to R15 (64-bit targets only). 4 is the stack pointer and is refused. On a 64-bit target 1 is the standard member call; Cheat Engine loads an integer argument 2, 3 or 4 into RDX, R8 or R9 and a fifth or later argument through RAX, so 2, 8, 9 and 0 are refused when that would overwrite this.

arguments.description: 0 to 16 typed arguments after this, as {type, value}: type is integer, float or double, and value is always a JSON string, even for integers ("10", not 10). Allocate and write text or buffers with memory_allocate and memory_write, then pass the allocation address as an integer.

type.description: integer (a 64-bit integer or pointer), float (32-bit) or double (64-bit); strings and buffers are not accepted.

value.description: The value as a JSON string, even for integer: "10", not 10. An integer is decimal, 0x-prefixed hexadecimal, or bare hexadecimal when it contains A-F; float and double take finite invariant text such as "1.5". At most 4096 characters.

functionAddress.description: The called function address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

returnValue.description: The function's integer return register (EAX or RAX) as Cheat Engine reported it, as decimal text.

name: exec_call_remote
title: Call target function
description: Call one function in the selected target with up to 16 numeric typed arguments, whose values are JSON strings even for integers. Allocate and write text or buffers with memory_allocate and memory_write, then pass the allocation address as an integer so it remains alive after a timeout. The function address is resolved through Client before Cheat Engine runs the fixed call body. Calls refuse a paused or debugger-stopped target and wait at most 10 seconds. A timeout or host refusal after the call begins has hostEffect unknown; inspect target state before retrying.

functionAddress.description: Address or Cheat Engine expression of the target function.

arguments.description: 0 to 16 typed arguments as {type, value}: type is integer, float or double, and value is always a JSON string, even for integers ("10", not 10). Allocate and write text or buffers with memory_allocate and memory_write, then pass the allocation address as an integer.

type.description: integer (a 64-bit integer or pointer), float (32-bit) or double (64-bit); strings and buffers are not accepted.

value.description: The value as a JSON string, even for integer: "10", not 10. An integer is decimal, 0x-prefixed hexadecimal, or bare hexadecimal when it contains A-F; float and double take finite invariant text such as "1.5". At most 4096 characters.

functionAddress.description: The called function address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

returnValue.description: The function's integer return register (EAX or RAX) as Cheat Engine reported it, as decimal text.

name: exec_compile_c
title: Compile C source
description: Compile up to 131072 characters of C source through Cheat Engine. Without address, Cheat Engine allocates memory in the selected target, or in itself with targetSelf, and writes the code there; kernelMode allocates kernel memory instead and requires Mcp:EnableKernelAccess. With address, Cheat Engine allocates nothing: it compiles for that address and writes the bytes there, overwriting what is there, so pass writable memory you own with room for the code, such as a memory_allocate allocation. Cheat Engine owns any allocation it made and exposes no general release API, so compile only code you intend to retain for this target session.

address.description: Optional write target in the selected process: Cheat Engine compiles for this address or expression and writes the bytes there without allocating. Only for targetSelf=false and without kernelMode.

targetSelf.description: Compile for Cheat Engine instead of the selected target.

kernelMode.description: Allocate the code in kernel memory through Cheat Engine's kernel driver; requires Mcp:EnableKernelAccess and applies only without address.

noDebug.description: Skip the source-line information Cheat Engine's debugger uses for the compiled code.

symbols.description: Up to 1024 compiled symbols, sorted by name.

address.description: The symbol's address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

symbolsTruncated.description: Whether the compiler produced more than 1024 symbols.

targetSelf.description: Whether the code was compiled into Cheat Engine's own process.

kernelMode.description: Whether the code was allocated in kernel memory.

name: exec_compile_csharp
title: Compile managed source
description: Compile up to 131072 characters of C# source with Cheat Engine's compileCS bridge and immediately copy its generated assembly to outputPath under an approved write root. The compiler uses the optional checked coreAssembly and up to 32 checked reference assemblies. Compilation does not inject or invoke the assembly. Cheat Engine owns its original generated file and may remove it when Cheat Engine, or another instance, closes; MCP never deletes that file. Compiler availability still depends on Cheat Engine's supported .NET Framework compiler prerequisites.

outputPath.description: Approved-root destination for the exported compiled assembly. It must not already exist unless overwrite is true.

referencePaths.description: 0 to 32 absolute local reference-assembly paths held against changes while Cheat Engine compiles.

coreAssembly.description: Optional absolute local core assembly path held against changes while Cheat Engine compiles.

overwrite.description: Allow the approved-root outputPath to atomically replace an existing file.

outputPath.description: The anchored approved-root path where MCP copied the compiled assembly.

length.description: The exported assembly length in bytes.

sha256.description: The uppercase SHA-256 hash of the exported assembly bytes.

name: exec_inject_dotnet
title: Inject managed assembly
description: Inject a managed assembly into the selected .NET Framework or .NET Core target and call its public static int method that takes one string. The absolute local path is checked and held while Cheat Engine opens it. Cheat Engine copies assemblyPath, className, methodName and parameter into fixed Auto Assembler strings, so control characters, quotes and braces are refused, as are more than 255 UTF-8 bytes for the path and 127 for the others. Cheat Engine then waits on its main thread, with no time limit, until the method returns: only the MCP call timeout (45 s by default in the gateway) bounds the request, and Cheat Engine stays blocked after it. A target with an active Cheat Engine Mono data collector is refused as unsupported. A timeout or failure after admission has hostEffect unknown; inspect the target before retrying.

assemblyPath.description: Absolute path of the managed assembly on the Cheat Engine host; at most 255 UTF-8 bytes without control characters, quotes or braces.

className.description: Namespace-qualified name of the type that declares the method, such as MyMod.Loader (nested types use +); 1 to 127 UTF-8 bytes without control characters, quotes or braces.

methodName.description: Name of a public static method declared as int Method(string); 1 to 127 UTF-8 bytes without control characters, quotes or braces.

parameter.description: String passed to the method; 0 to 127 UTF-8 bytes without control characters, quotes or braces.

assemblyPath.description: The checked full path Cheat Engine loaded.

className.description: The type name that declares the called method.

result.description: The method's signed int return value as decimal text, such as "-1"; Cheat Engine reads it back unsigned and MCP restores the sign.

name: exec_inject_library
title: Inject native library
description: Inject a native DLL or library into the selected target. The absolute local path is checked and held against changes while Cheat Engine opens it; protected MCP folders and links are refused. Injection can load target code and cannot be undone by MCP. A failure after admission has hostEffect unknown; inspect the target before retrying.

libraryPath.description: Absolute path of the native library on the Cheat Engine host.

skipSymbolReloadWait.description: Do not wait for Cheat Engine to reload symbols after injection.

libraryPath.description: The checked full path Cheat Engine injected.

skippedSymbolReloadWait.description: Whether Cheat Engine was told not to wait for its symbol reload after the injection.

name: kernel_get_status
title: Get DBK and DBVM status
description: Read whether DBK and DBVM are already initialized, plus any CR0, CR3, CR4 and DBVM real-CR4 values that Cheat Engine can read. It does not load a driver or initialize DBVM. Null register values are unavailable, not zero; call this before any kernel operation.

name: kernel_initialize_dbvm
title: Initialize DBVM
description: Initialize DBVM. With offloadOperatingSystem=false (the default) Cheat Engine loads nothing: the call only confirms that DBVM already runs and otherwise fails with invalid_state and hostEffect not_started. With offloadOperatingSystem=true, when DBVM is not yet running and the CPU can run it, Cheat Engine first loads its DBK kernel driver without any prompt, then shows a confirmation dialog that a human must answer: Cheat Engine's own crash warning followed by reason. Loading DBVM can freeze or blue-screen the host. Never retry an unknown outcome: call kernel_get_status after the host responds.

offloadOperatingSystem.description: false only confirms that DBVM already runs and loads nothing; true loads DBK, then DBVM after a human confirms, which can crash the host.

reason.description: Short operator-facing reason, at most 256 characters. With offloadOperatingSystem=true the dialog shows it after Cheat Engine's own crash warning.

dbvmInitialized.description: Always true: Cheat Engine confirmed that DBVM runs; any other outcome is an error.

reason.description: The caller's reason as passed; omitted when none was given.

name: kernel_poll_watch
title: Poll DBVM watch
description: Poll one DBVM watch job. The first call uses afterSequence=0, then returns nextAfterSequence for the next page. Each call first moves every event DBVM logged since the previous call into the job's bounded ring (DBVM empties its log on each retrieval), then returns a non-consuming page with the refreshed job status; dropped counts events evicted from that ring. Events DBVM discarded because internalEntryCount filled between polls are not reported, so poll often; events logged after the last poll are lost when the job ends. Events include only a bounded register projection, never FPU or stack snapshots. Stop with runtime_stop_job(jobId), which disables the watch.

afterSequence.description: 0 first, then nextAfterSequence from the previous response.

job.description: The watch job status, refreshed from Cheat Engine by this poll.

jobId.description: The job id.

state.description: Where the job stands.

expiresInMs.description: Milliseconds until its TTL ends and its results are discarded.

buffered.description: How many items are retained for polling.

total.description: How many items the job produced; the last sequence number.

dropped.description: How many of the oldest items were evicted because the buffer was full.

createdUtc.description: When the job started, in UTC, when known.

progressDone.description: How much work is done, in the job's own unit.

progressTotal.description: How much work there is, when known.

error.description: Why the job failed or ended early.

cleanupError.description: Why its cleanup failed; it then needs manual recovery and an acknowledgement.

requiresManualRecovery.description: Whether something may remain that only manual recovery can remove.

processId.description: The process selected when the job started, when known.

sourceIndex.description: The 1-based position of the event among all events DBVM returned for this watch; it equals its job sequence.

name: kernel_read_physical
title: Read physical memory
description: Read 1 to 4096 bytes from a literal physical address through DBVM. The whole range must stay inside the unsigned 64-bit physical-address space. Physical memory can belong to Windows, a driver or another process, and a translation can go stale; prefer memory_read for normal target memory and call kernel_translate_address again just before this operation.

size.description: Number of bytes to read, 1 to 4096.

name: kernel_start_watch
title: Start DBVM watch
description: Start a DBVM physical-page watch as a bounded job. The watched range must stay inside one 4 KiB physical page: (physicalAddress & 0xFFF) + byteSize may not exceed 4096, because DBVM silently shortens a range that crosses a page boundary. The watch observes every process and kernel access to the physical page. Poll it with kernel_poll_watch; runtime_stop_job(jobId), TTL expiry and plugin shutdown run its Lua cleanup hook to disable the DBVM watch. options may use only bits 0 to 3, because options 5 and above can create unbounded DBVM logs or change execution.

access.description: read, write or execute. A read watch also reports writes, as Cheat Engine documents.

physicalAddress.description: Literal physical hexadecimal address to watch.

byteSize.description: Watched byte size, 1 to 4096, without crossing a 4 KiB physical page boundary.

options.description: DBVM watch option bits 0 to 3 only.

internalEntryCount.description: Maximum entries DBVM retains internally, 1 to 4096.

lifetimeSeconds.description: Watch job lifetime in seconds, 1 to 300; default from Mcp:Execution.

bufferLimit.description: Events retained in the MCP job buffer, 1 to Mcp:Execution:JobBufferLimit, which is also the default; older events are evicted and counted in dropped.

name: kernel_translate_address
title: Translate virtual address
description: Translate one virtual address in the selected target to its current physical address through DBK. The virtual expression is resolved with Client before the fixed DBK call. Translate one page at a time immediately before access: physical mappings can change or cease to be resident.

address.description: Virtual target address or Cheat Engine expression.

name: kernel_write_physical
title: Write physical memory
description: Write 1 to 4096 hexadecimal bytes to a literal physical address through DBVM, bypassing page protection. The whole range must stay inside the unsigned 64-bit physical-address space. The range may back Windows, a driver or another process. A failed call after admission has hostEffect unknown; read the physical range before attempting another write or a restore.

bytes.description: Hexadecimal bytes, for example 48 8B 05; at most 4096 bytes.

name: lua_execute
title: Execute Lua
description: Execute caller-authored Lua through Cheat Engine's unsafe Lua capability. source is compiled as text and runs synchronously on Cheat Engine's main thread, so it can freeze Cheat Engine, change the target or host, access files and network, create state that MCP cannot track, or show a dialog that waits for a person. Returned values are copied with bounds: functions, userdata and CE objects are dropped. Use a dedicated tool whenever one exists; this tool requires Mcp:EnableUnsafeLua.

source.description: Lua 5.3 source, up to 1048576 UTF-8 bytes. It runs with Cheat Engine's full Lua API.

chunkName.description: An optional non-empty Lua chunk name for diagnostics, up to 256 UTF-8 bytes.

phase.description: compile or runtime when Ok is false.

error.description: The Lua compiler or runtime message when Ok is false.

hostEffect.description: The confirmed effect of the caller chunk: completed on success, not_applied after a compile error, or unknown after a runtime error.

returnValues.description: Every returned Lua value in order; opaque values are represented as null or omitted from objects.

droppedOpaqueCount.description: Functions, userdata and threads omitted while copying returned values.

name: lua_find_api
title: Find Lua API
description: Search the celua.txt Lua API reference in this Cheat Engine installation, case-insensitively. Returns matching lines with their source line numbers, at most 100 per page. The file is read only from Cheat Engine's own installation directory, is never returned in full and is bounded to 4 MiB and 65536 lines; a source-file bound returns the bounded prefix with truncated true and no nextOffset. Use a specific function or class name and page with nextOffset.

query.description: A case-insensitive Lua function, class or API term of 1 to 256 UTF-8 bytes, such as getAddressSafe.

limit.description: The number of matching lines to return, from 1 to 100.

offset.description: The zero-based offset among matching lines from a previous nextOffset.

total.description: The matching lines found in celua.txt, or in its bounded prefix when truncated is true.

name: memory_allocate
title: Allocate memory
description: Allocate target memory under a caller-chosen name, read and write by default or executable for code (up to 16 MiB each, 128 allocations and 64 MiB per activation). The allocation is an activation resource: free it with memory_free or runtime_release_resources before switching processes; disabling the plugin frees it too.

name.description: A unique name for the allocation, 1 to 256 characters; memory_free takes it back.

size.description: The number of bytes to allocate, 1 to 16777216; Cheat Engine may round it up to a page.

executable.description: Whether the memory is executable (read, write and execute), for injected code.

near.description: An address or expression near which Cheat Engine should allocate, for code that jumps with a 32-bit displacement; Cheat Engine may allocate elsewhere.

name.description: The caller's name for the allocation; pass it to memory_free.

address.description: The allocated address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

size.description: The requested size in bytes; Cheat Engine may round the allocation up to a page.

executable.description: Whether the memory is executable (read, write and execute) rather than read and write.

resourceId.description: The id under which runtime_list_resources lists the allocation.

name: memory_compare
title: Compare memory
description: Compare two target ranges of up to 16 MiB and list the differing runs with both byte sequences. Reads 1 MiB per Cheat Engine dispatch and fails with target_changed if Cheat Engine selects another process in between; stops once maxDifferences runs are listed.

addressA.description: The first address or Cheat Engine address expression.

addressB.description: The second address or Cheat Engine address expression.

addressB.description: The resolved second address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

a.description: The bytes of the run at addressA, spaced hexadecimal.

b.description: The bytes of the run at addressB, spaced hexadecimal.

name: memory_compare_snapshot
title: Compare a memory snapshot
description: Compare a snapshot slot by slot, reading each slot as valueType every alignment bytes, with another snapshot of the same size (compareTo: no Cheat Engine call; the addresses may differ, so two objects compare field by field) or with live memory at the snapshot's address (compareTo omitted: 1 MiB per dispatch; target_changed once Cheat Engine selected another target since the snapshot). change keeps changed or unchanged slots by their bytes, or increased or decreased slots by numeric order (NaN never matches). Slots touching unreadable bytes on either side are skipped and counted. A live comparison reads memory again on every call, so its pages can shift; for stable paging, take a second snapshot and compare the two.

name.description: The snapshot to compare; its bytes are the before values.

compareTo.description: Another snapshot of the same size whose bytes are the after values; omit it to compare with live memory.

valueType.description: The type each slot is read as: int8 to uint64, float, double or pointer (default int32).

alignment.description: The distance between two slots from offset 0: 1, 2, 4 or 8, at most the size of valueType (default that size).

change.description: The slots to keep: changed (default) or unchanged by bytes, increased or decreased by numeric order.

offset.description: The zero-based index of the first matching slot to return.

limit.description: The most matching slots to return, 1 to 1000.

name.description: The compared snapshot, whose bytes are the before values.

address.description: The compared snapshot's address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

valueType.description: The type each slot is read as.

alignment.description: The distance in bytes between two slots, starting at offset 0.

change.description: The change filter: changed, unchanged, increased or decreased.

skipped.description: How many slots were skipped because they touch bytes that were unreadable on either side.

total.description: How many compared slots match the change filter.

changes.description: The matching slots of this page, in offset order.

address.description: The slot's address in the compared snapshot, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

offset.description: The slot's offset from the snapshot's address, hexadecimal.

before.description: The slot's value in the compared snapshot, as text of valueType.

after.description: The slot's value in compareTo or in live memory, as text of valueType.

compareTo.description: The other snapshot, whose bytes are the after values; omitted when live memory was compared.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; omitted when this page ends the listing.

name: memory_copy
title: Copy memory
description: Copy up to 1 MiB from one target address to another: the whole source is read first, so overlapping ranges copy correctly. The destination is overwritten; allocate it with memory_allocate when it must be new memory.

source.description: The source address or Cheat Engine address expression.

destination.description: The destination address or Cheat Engine address expression.

size.description: The number of bytes to copy, 1 to 1048576.

source.description: The resolved source address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

destination.description: The resolved destination address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

size.description: The number of bytes copied.

name: memory_create_snapshot
title: Create a memory snapshot
description: Copy up to 16 MiB of target memory into a named snapshot that this activation holds in managed memory (not a target resource; at most 16 snapshots and 64 MiB in total, else limit_exceeded; a taken name fails with invalid_state). Reads 1 MiB per Cheat Engine dispatch and fails with target_changed if Cheat Engine selects another process in between. Unreadable memory is stored as zeros, listed, and skipped by comparisons. Take a snapshot, act in the target, then call memory_compare_snapshot. Snapshots survive a process switch, but compare with live memory only while the same target stays selected; free them with memory_delete_snapshot.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression, such as game.exe+1C or [player]+10.

size.description: The number of bytes to copy, 1 to 16777216.

name.description: The snapshot's name; pass it to memory_compare_snapshot and memory_delete_snapshot.

address.description: The resolved start address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

size.description: The number of bytes copied.

processId.description: The process the snapshot was taken from.

name: memory_delete_snapshot
title: Delete a memory snapshot

The path must be absolute, local and inside a folder listed in Mcp:Files:AllowedRoots (empty by default, which refuses every dump); the MCP data and registry folders are always refused. Reads 1 MiB per dispatch into a temporary file that replaces the target file only when complete; unreadable memory fails the dump unless unreadable is zero.

name: memory_get_address_info

An address that does not resolve reports its own error in band.

name: memory_read_samples
title: Sample values over time
description: Read up to 64 addresses as one fixed-size value type every intervalMs for durationMs (at most 10 s from the first read, so the call returns within about that time), for example to find which scan result follows a value while it changes in the target. Addresses are resolved once; each tick is one short Cheat Engine dispatch, and the call waits between ticks without holding Cheat Engine's main thread. Each series keeps its first value and every change, at most 256 points with their time since the first read, plus first, last and distinct counts. An address that does not resolve or cannot be read reports its error in band; a later tick that Cheat Engine refuses as busy is skipped and counted in missedTicks. Fails with target_changed if Cheat Engine selects another process between ticks.

It is refused while the target is paused or the debugger is stopped.

The collector DLL, the mono_error_ok patch and the table Uses Mono option remain. An attachment Cheat Engine or the user made is never closed: when this activation's attachment already ended (a detach, re-activation or target switch in Cheat Engine), only its MCP resource is released and alreadyEnded is true.

name: mono_get_object
title: Get Mono object
description: Identify the Mono or IL2CPP object that contains an address, such as a value found by a scan, and read its fields with their current values. The object start is searched from the address down to maxBacktrack bytes below it by reading target memory only: the nearest header must lead to a class the collector lists in that class's own image (through the vtable on Mono, directly on IL2CPP), so the collector is never asked about an unverified address, which can crash the target. Objects of generic instance and array classes are refused as unsupported, and so are objects whose image an IL2CPP collector cannot list classes for (Cheat Engine's memory-scan guess of that list is not used). Fields include inherited and static ones, with values read like dotnet_get_object. Enumerating the classes of the object's image can block Cheat Engine for seconds on a large assembly.

The first speed other than 1 in a process activates the speedhack, which can inject code into the target or show a Cheat Engine dialog. Once the speedhack_wantedspeed symbol exists, Cheat Engine never hooks that process again, even after a failed hook, so hooksInstalled does not prove working hooks. While speed differs from 1, MCP tracks a resource that runtime_release_resources restores to 1 before a target change. Speed 1 never activates the speedhack or removes hooks: it restores 1 only where that symbol exists, does nothing while Cheat Engine's and the target's speed are 1, and refuses (invalid_state) when Cheat Engine reports another speed for a process without the symbol. The call is refused (invalid_state) without an attached process, and a change also while the target is paused or stopped in the debugger. While hooksInstalled is false after a failed activation, a retry attempts the hooks again.

Speed 1 never activates the speedhack and always reports false. If the attempt failed after creating the symbol, Cheat Engine never retries in this process; if hooksInstalled is still false, a later call retries.

resourceId.description: The MCP-owned resource that restores speed to 1 through runtime_release_resources; omitted at speed 1.

name: structure_add_elements
title: Add structure elements
description: Adds elements to a structure, all or nothing: when Cheat Engine refuses one, the elements this call added are removed again. Cheat Engine orders elements by offset, so indices returns where each added element landed.

elements.description: The elements to add (1-256); offsets are signed hexadecimal.

offset.description: The offset from the structure's start, as signed hexadecimal such as 4C8 or -8.

name.description: The element's name, up to 256 characters; may be empty.

valueType.description: The element's value type.

display.description: How to display an integer element: signed for intN, unsigned or hex for uintN; defaults to the type's signedness.

byteSize.description: The byte size of a string, wstring or bytes element (1-65536); required for them, refused otherwise.

childStructure.description: The name of the structure a pointer element points to; pointer elements only.

childStructureStart.description: Where the pointer lands inside the child structure, as signed hexadecimal; default 0.

size.description: The bytes from the structure's start to the end of its last element.

elementCount.description: The number of elements after the change.

indices.description: The indices of the added or updated elements after Cheat Engine reordered them by offset, or the removed indices.

name: structure_autoguess
title: Auto-guess a structure
description: Lets Cheat Engine guess element types from the current bytes at address plus offset, like the dissect window's automatic guess, creating the structure when missing. The guessed elements are added from offset on and existing elements are kept, so guess into a range that has none yet. Guesses are unconfirmed: pointers can read as integers and padding as fields. Keep size to the object, usually 1024-4096 bytes.

address.description: The object's base address or symbol expression, such as 7FF6A1B2C3D0 or [game.exe+1C]+10; the bytes are read from this address plus offset.

offset.description: The structure offset where guessing starts, as hexadecimal, zero or greater: Cheat Engine reads from address plus offset and places the first guessed element at this offset.

size.description: The bytes to guess from, a decimal count (1-65536).

createIfMissing.description: Create the structure when no structure has this name.

size.description: The bytes from the structure's start to the end of its last element.

name: structure_compare
title: Compare structure instances
description: Compares instances byte for byte, like the dissect window's group compare, to find a field that separates group A (such as the player) from group B (enemies). Rows are cells of granularity bytes over size bytes, or the elements of structureName. Each row is constant, discriminator (constant inside each group, different between them), varies_a, varies_b, varies_both or unreadable; mode picks which rows return. Validate a discriminator with more samples before relying on it.

groupA.description: Group A's base addresses or symbol expressions (1-32).

groupB.description: Group B's base addresses or symbol expressions (0-32); discriminate needs at least one.

size.description: The bytes to compare from each base, a decimal count (1-16384) that is a multiple of granularity; pass this or structureName.

structureName.description: Compare along this structure's elements instead of raw cells; pass this or size.

granularity.description: The cell size in bytes for size mode: 1, 2, 4 or 8.

interpretAs.description: How size-mode cells read: auto, signed, unsigned, float (granularity 4 or 8) or hex.

mode.description: Which rows to return: discriminate, constant, differs (not equal everywhere) or all.

offset.description: The zero-based index of the first selected row to return.

groupA.description: The resolved addresses of group A.

groupB.description: The resolved addresses of group B.

offset.description: The field's offset, as signed hexadecimal.

size.description: The field's size in bytes.

classification.description: What the field shows across the groups.

valuesA.description: The field in each instance of group A, in request order; null when unreadable.

valuesB.description: The field in each instance of group B, in request order; null when unreadable.

name.description: The element's name when comparing along a structure; omitted otherwise.

total.description: The number of rows the mode selects.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; omitted when the listing is complete.

name: structure_create
title: Create a structure
description: Creates a global structure from at most one source: explicit elements, a copy of cloneFrom, or the PDB type pdbTypeName of the loaded symbols; with none it is empty. It is all or nothing and refuses an existing name. The structure persists in Cheat Engine and is saved with the table; delete what you created with structure_delete.

name.description: The new structure's case-sensitive name; it must not exist yet.

elements.description: The elements to create (at most 1024); offsets are signed hexadecimal.

offset.description: The offset from the structure's start, as signed hexadecimal such as 4C8 or -8.

name.description: The element's name, up to 256 characters; may be empty.

valueType.description: The element's value type.

display.description: How to display an integer element: signed for intN, unsigned or hex for uintN; defaults to the type's signedness.

byteSize.description: The byte size of a string, wstring or bytes element (1-65536); required for them, refused otherwise.

childStructure.description: The name of the structure a pointer element points to; pointer elements only.

childStructureStart.description: Where the pointer lands inside the child structure, as signed hexadecimal; default 0.

cloneFrom.description: The name of an existing structure to copy.

pdbTypeName.description: The name of a type in the loaded PDB symbols; check it with structure_get_pdb_layout first.

internal.description: Create an internal structure: selectable as a child structure, but hidden from the structure list and not saved with the table.

size.description: The bytes from the structure's start to the end of its last element.

name: structure_delete
title: Delete a structure
description: Deletes a structure from Cheat Engine; pointer elements of other structures that pointed to it lose their child structure. Delete only structures you created, unless the user asks. An unknown name is not_found.

name: structure_fill_from_dotnet
title: Fill a structure from .NET
description: Adds the fields of the managed object at address, as Cheat Engine's .NET data collector reports them, to a structure, creating it when missing; give the object's address, not a field's. It refuses with busy while the target is paused or stopped in the debugger, and with not_found when no .NET layout is found. The query runs out of process and can block Cheat Engine for a few seconds.

address.description: The managed object's address or symbol expression.

rename.description: Rename the structure to the object's .NET class name.

createIfMissing.description: Create the structure when no structure has this name.

size.description: The bytes from the structure's start to the end of its last element.

name: structure_generate_c_header
title: Generate a C header
description: Writes C declarations for structures and every child structure their pointer elements reach: forward typedefs, then each structure with padding for gaps. By default Cheat Engine's own generator writes them, as its Export to C header file menu does. managed writes fixed-width types, offset comments, pack(1) and commented size checks, sizes byte-array, bit-field and custom elements exactly (Cheat Engine writes an int), and is the fallback when Cheat Engine's generator is missing or fails or the elements span more than 1 MiB. At most 256 structures, 8192 elements and 1 MiB of text.

names.description: The distinct case-sensitive names of the structures to declare (1-64).

generator.description: cheat_engine or managed; omit to use Cheat Engine's generator when it has one and managed otherwise.

text.description: The C declarations, at most 1 MiB of UTF-8.

generator.description: Which generator wrote the text: cheat_engine or managed.

structures.description: The structures the text declares: the requested ones, then the child structures their pointers reach.

name: structure_get
title: Get a structure
description: Reads one structure, internal ones included, and a page of its elements ordered by offset: index, hexadecimal offset, name, valueType, integer display, byteSize and child structure. The detailed format adds the child start, custom type and bit fields.

offset.description: The zero-based index of the first element to return.

format.description: concise, or detailed for the child start, custom type and bit fields.

size.description: The bytes from the structure's start to the end of its last element.

internal.description: Whether the structure is internal: selectable as a child but hidden and never saved.

index.description: The element's zero-based index; elements are ordered by offset.

offset.description: The element's offset from the structure's start, as signed hexadecimal.

name.description: The element's name; may be empty.

valueType.description: The element's value type.

display.description: How Cheat Engine displays an integer element; omitted for other types.

childStructure.description: The structure a pointer element points to; omitted when none.

childStructureStart.description: Where the pointer lands inside the child structure, as signed hexadecimal; detailed format only.

customType.description: The name of a custom element's custom type; detailed format only.

bitStart.description: The first bit of a binary element; detailed format only.

bitSize.description: The bit count of a binary element; detailed format only.

total.description: The number of elements in the whole structure.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; omitted when the listing is complete.

name: structure_get_pdb_layout
title: Get a PDB structure layout
description: Reads the fields of a type from the loaded PDB symbols: offset, name and value type. found is false when the symbols do not describe it; load a PDB with symbol_add_module(enumStructures=true). Create a structure from it with structure_create(pdbTypeName).

typeName.description: The PDB type name, such as _PEB.

found.description: Whether the loaded symbols describe the type.

elements.description: The type's fields, in Cheat Engine's order.

offset.description: The field's offset, as signed hexadecimal.

valueType.description: The field's value type; omitted when Cheat Engine reports none.

truncated.description: Whether the type has more fields than the limit.

name: structure_list
title: List structures
description: Pages Cheat Engine's global Structure Dissect definitions: name, size and element count. Structures are shared with the user and saved in the cheat table; check a name here before creating one.

nameContains.description: Only structures whose name contains this text, ignoring case; omit for all.

offset.description: The zero-based index of the first structure to return.

size.description: The bytes from the structure's start to the end of its last element.

total.description: The number of structures that match the filter.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; omitted when the listing is complete.

truncated.description: Whether a host-side cap stopped the enumeration of global structures.

name: structure_read
title: Read structure values
description: Reads a page of a structure's elements at up to 16 base addresses, like Cheat Engine's dissect window: one column per address and one row per element, values in the contract format of the element's valueType, null where unreadable. fromOffset and toOffset keep only elements in that offset range; one page spans at most 65536 bytes.

addresses.description: The base addresses or symbol expressions (1-16), one column each.

fromOffset.description: Only elements at or after this offset, as signed hexadecimal.

toOffset.description: Only elements at or before this offset, as signed hexadecimal.

offset.description: The zero-based index of the first element of the range to return.

format.description: concise, or detailed to add each element's byteSize, display and raw bytes.

columns.description: One column per base address, in request order.

address.description: The resolved base address.

confirmedLength.description: The bytes Cheat Engine confirmed readable from the lowest element offset of the page; elements past it read as null.

elements.description: One row per element of this page.

offset.description: The element's offset, as signed hexadecimal.

valueType.description: The element's value type.

values.description: The value at each column's address, in column order; integers in decimal, pointers in hexadecimal, null when unreadable.

byteSize.description: The bytes the element occupies; detailed format only.

display.description: How Cheat Engine displays an integer element; detailed format only.

raw.description: The element's bytes at each column's address, null when unreadable; detailed format only.

total.description: The number of elements in the offset range.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; omitted when the listing is complete.

name: structure_remove_elements
title: Remove structure elements
description: Removes elements by their current indices, highest first so the others keep their index. Every index is checked first; a refusal stops the batch with partial_effect. indices returns the removed indices.

indices.description: The distinct zero-based indices to remove (1-256), from structure_get.

size.description: The bytes from the structure's start to the end of its last element.

elementCount.description: The number of elements after the change.

indices.description: The indices of the added or updated elements after Cheat Engine reordered them by offset, or the removed indices.

name: structure_set_name
title: Rename a structure
description: Renames a structure in place, internal ones included; pointer elements of other structures keep pointing to it, unlike a copy with structure_create(cloneFrom) and a delete. A newName that any structure already has is invalid_state; the current name is a no-op. A global structure is saved with the table under its new name; an internal structure is never saved.

newName.description: The new case-sensitive name (1-256 characters); no other structure may have it.

size.description: The bytes from the structure's start to the end of its last element.

name: structure_update_elements
title: Update structure elements
description: Renames, retypes or moves elements. Every update names a different element by its index before this call; all are checked first, then applied in order. The first refusal stops the batch with partial_effect (details.applied, details.failedIndex); read the structure with structure_get before retrying the rest.

updates.description: The updates (1-256), at most one per element; each sets at least one field.

index.description: The element's zero-based index before this call, from structure_get.

offset.description: A new offset, as signed hexadecimal; omit to keep it.

name.description: A new name, up to 256 characters; omit to keep it.

valueType.description: A new value type; omit to keep it. String, wstring and bytes also need byteSize.

display.description: A new display for an integer element; omit to keep it or to follow a new valueType.

byteSize.description: A new byte size (1-65536) for a string, wstring or bytes element; omit to keep it.

size.description: The bytes from the structure's start to the end of its last element.

elementCount.description: The number of elements after the change.

indices.description: The indices of the added or updated elements after Cheat Engine reordered them by offset, or the removed indices.

name: structure_write_element
title: Write a structure element
description: Writes value into the target at address plus the element's offset, encoded as the element's valueType (integers in decimal or 0x hexadecimal, pointers in hexadecimal, bytes as 48 8B 05, text with a terminator when it fits), then reads it back. Bit fields and custom types use Cheat Engine's own text format. It is a mutation: after an error, check hostEffect before trying again.

address.description: The structure instance's base address or symbol expression.

index.description: The element's zero-based index, from structure_get.

value.description: The value to write, in the format of the element's valueType.

address.description: The element's address: the base address plus the element's offset.

size.description: The bytes written.

value.description: The value read back after the write; omitted when the read-back failed.

name: symbol_add_module
title: Load symbols from a file
description: Load the symbols of a file, such as a game-shipped PDB or a DLL, as a module at baseAddress (Cheat Engine's symbolHandlerAddModule). enumStructures also enumerates PDB structures for structure_get_pdb_layout. path must be an absolute path on a local fixed drive; UNC, device and linked paths, alternate streams and the MCP directories are refused, and the file stays locked against changes during the load. One native call: a large PDB blocks Cheat Engine for several seconds (blocking_native).

path.description: The absolute path of the symbol file on a local fixed drive, such as C:\Games\Game\game.pdb.

baseAddress.description: The base address the symbols apply to, as an address expression such as game.exe or 7FF6A1B20000.

enumStructures.description: Also enumerate PDB structures, which structure_get_pdb_layout reads; slower.

path.description: The normalized path of the loaded file.

base.description: The base address the symbols were loaded at, as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

enumStructures.description: Whether PDB structures were enumerated for structure_get_pdb_layout.

name: symbol_enable_sources
title: Enable system symbol sources
description: Enable Windows PDB symbols and/or kernel export symbols in Cheat Engine. Windows symbols can download PDBs from an external symbol service and block for a long time on first use. Kernel symbols require Mcp:EnableKernelAccess. Returns which sources were requested and whether external network access may have occurred.

windows.description: Enable Windows PDB symbols; may download files from an external service.

kernel.description: Enable kernel symbols; requires the kernel access switch.

name: symbol_find
title: Find symbols
description: Find symbols whose names contain nameContains, matched literally and ASCII case-insensitively, such as Health or CreateFile. It searches registered symbols, registered symbol lists ({$C} Auto Assembler functions, IL2CPP methods) and the main symbol list (exports; PDB symbols of the game or from symbol_add_module or symbol_enable_sources); .NET, Mono JIT and module names are not searched. module keeps only symbols inside one loaded module. Matches are sorted by name, then address; at most 10000 are collected (truncated says more match), then offset and limit (at most 500) page them, each with its module and size when known. symbolsLoaded=false means Cheat Engine is still loading symbols or IL2CPP methods: repeat later before concluding a name is absent. Every call copies all these lists on Cheat Engine's main thread, whatever the filters: quick with exports and a game PDB, but with Windows PDB symbols or IL2CPP methods loaded it can block Cheat Engine for a second or more (host_scan).

nameContains.description: The text to find in symbol names, 2 to 128 characters, matched literally and ASCII case-insensitively, such as Health.

module.description: Keep only symbols inside this loaded module: a name such as game.exe or an address inside it; omit to search all.

offset.description: The index of the first sorted match to return.

limit.description: The most matches to return, 1 to 500.

total.description: The number of matches collected, at most 10000; see truncated.

truncated.description: Whether the search stopped at 10000 matches, so more symbols match and the collected ones are an arbitrary subset; narrow nameContains or pass module.

symbolsLoaded.description: Whether Cheat Engine reported every symbol loaded, and any IL2CPP method list fully enumerated, before the search; while false a name missing now may appear later.

symbols.description: The matches of this page, sorted by lowercase name, then name, then address.

name.description: The symbol name as Cheat Engine lists it; use it in any address expression.

address.description: The symbol's address as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

module.description: The module that defines the symbol, as Cheat Engine names it; omitted when it does not say.

size.description: The symbol's size in bytes, or a registered allocation's size; omitted when unknown or zero, and for the size 1 Cheat Engine gives symbols of registered symbol lists by default.

registered.description: True for a symbol registered by a table, a script (including {$C} code and other registered symbol lists) or symbol_register; omitted for loaded symbols.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; omitted on the last page.

name: symbol_get_module_preference
title: Get module preference
description: Read Cheat Engine's module precedence for symbol lookup: when a symbol name exists in several modules, the first listed module wins. Names are extensionless; at most 1024 are returned.

modules.description: Extensionless module names; a symbol present in several modules resolves in the first listed one.

truncated.description: Whether Cheat Engine's list is longer than the 1024 names copied.

name: symbol_list_registered
title: List registered symbols
description: Page every symbol registered in Cheat Engine (by tables, Auto Assembler scripts, Lua and this plugin), marking with ownedByMcp the ones this activation registered and can unregister. Allocation symbols carry their size. Filter with nameContains, then page with offset and limit (at most 1000); at most 8192 symbols are copied.

nameContains.description: A case-insensitive substring of the symbol name; at most 256 characters.

offset.description: The index of the first symbol to return.

limit.description: The most symbols to return, 1 to 1000.

total.description: The number of copied symbols that match nameContains.

truncated.description: Whether Cheat Engine holds more than the 8192 symbols that were copied.

symbols.description: The symbols of this page, in Cheat Engine's order.

ownedByMcp.description: Whether this plugin activation registered it (symbol_register); only those can be unregistered.

address.description: The address it names, as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

doNotSave.description: Whether a saved cheat table omits the symbol; omitted when false.

allocSize.description: The size of the allocation it names, for an Auto Assembler alloc; omitted otherwise.

processId.description: The process of that allocation; omitted otherwise.

resourceId.description: The resource id of an owned symbol, as runtime_list_resources reports it.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; omitted on the last page.

name: symbol_register
title: Register a symbol
description: Register a named symbol, such as playerBase, for an address, so later address expressions, records and scripts can use the name. The address expression is resolved once, now. The symbol is owned by this plugin activation: at most 128 at a time; symbol_unregister, runtime_release_resources or disabling the plugin removes it. A name that already resolves in Cheat Engine (another symbol, a module or a hexadecimal number) is refused. doNotSave (default true) keeps it out of saved cheat tables.

name.description: The symbol name, 1 to 256 characters; use a distinctive name such as playerBase.

address.description: The address it names, as an address expression such as [game.exe+1A2B]+10 or 7FF6A1B2C3D0.

doNotSave.description: Keep the symbol out of saved cheat tables.

name.description: The symbol name; use it in any address expression.

address.description: The address it names, as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

doNotSave.description: Whether a saved cheat table omits the symbol.

resourceId.description: The id runtime_list_resources reports for it; runtime_release_resources and symbol_unregister release it.

name: symbol_reload
title: Reload symbols
description: Start a symbol reload and return at once; it never waits. new_modules loads the symbols of modules loaded since the last scan, all reinitializes the whole symbol handler, dotnet reinitializes the .NET symbols (after code was JIT-compiled), optionally of one module. done tells whether Cheat Engine reports every symbol loaded; while it is false, poll runtime_get_overview (symbolsLoaded) instead of waiting.

module.description: The .NET module to reinitialize, such as Assembly-CSharp.dll; only with scope dotnet.

done.description: Whether Cheat Engine reports every symbol loaded; false while loading continues in the background.

scope.description: The reload that was started: new_modules, all or dotnet.

name: symbol_resolve
title: Resolve addresses and names
description: Resolve up to 256 Cheat Engine expressions in one call. Each expression may be an address (7FF6A1B2C3D0), a module offset (game.exe+1A2B), an export (kernel32.CreateFileW), a registered symbol or pointer arithmetic ([game.exe+10]+8). Each entry returns the address, Cheat Engine's best name for it (module+offset or symbol) and the symbol record when the expression names one. An expression that does not resolve carries its own error; check every entry. shallow skips the slower lookups, such as symbols still loading.

name.description: Cheat Engine's best name for the address: a registered symbol, module.export or module+offset.

symbol.description: The symbol record, when the expression names a symbol Cheat Engine knows.

module.description: The module that defines the symbol.

key.description: The symbol's search key, its name without the module.

address.description: The symbol's address as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

size.description: The symbol's size in bytes, zero when unknown.

error.description: Why this expression did not resolve; the other entries are unaffected.

kind.description: The failure class, such as not_found.

name: symbol_set_module_preference
title: Set module preference
description: Change Cheat Engine's module precedence for symbol lookup. By default the given modules move to the front in the given order and the rest of the current list follows; replace=true makes them the whole list, dropping the others. Names are extensionless (game, not game.exe). Returns the list read back. It affects every later lookup in this Cheat Engine, tables included.

modules.description: 1 to 64 extensionless module names, first first, such as ["game", "engine"].

replace.description: Replace the whole list instead of moving these modules to the front.

modules.description: Extensionless module names; a symbol present in several modules resolves in the first listed one.

truncated.description: Whether Cheat Engine's list is longer than the 1024 names copied.

name: symbol_unregister
title: Unregister a symbol
description: Unregister a symbol that this plugin activation registered with symbol_register. A name this activation does not own is not_found, including symbols of tables and scripts. An incomplete release is a partial_effect error whose details carry the release outcome: retryable means nothing happened yet and the call can be repeated; otherwise manual recovery is needed.

name.description: The symbol name, as symbol_register returned it (case-insensitive).

address.description: The address it named, as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

requiresManualRecovery.description: Whether something may remain that only manual recovery can remove.

name: table_list_files
title: List table files
description: List .CT, .XML and .CETRAINER files below the configured CheatEngineClient:AllowedTableRoots. The enumeration skips inaccessible and reparse-pointed entries, considers at most 10000 files, and returns absolute paths suitable for table_load. An empty roots list means Client will refuse every table load and save.

offset.description: The requested zero-based offset.

size.description: The file size in bytes.

lastWriteUtc.description: The file's last-write time in UTC.

nextOffset.description: The next offset within the retained page set, omitted after its final page.

name: table_load
title: Load cheat table
description: Inspect and load a .CT, .XML or .CETRAINER file through CheatEngine.Client. The source is pinned while inspected and loaded, and Client independently enforces CheatEngineClient:AllowedTableRoots. The inspection derives and enforces capability gates before Cheat Engine can execute Lua, Auto Assembler records or a Mono auto attach. A native load failure can leave a partial table or script effect.

path.description: The absolute local table path. CheatEngineClient:AllowedTableRoots must admit it.

merge.description: Whether to merge into the existing address list rather than replace it.

path.description: The absolute table path admitted by CheatEngine.Client's allowed table roots.

merge.description: Whether Cheat Engine merged the table into the existing address list.

inspection.description: The inspection that ran while the source file was pinned.

format.description: xml when completely inspected, or the opaque format that forced a conservative policy.

containsLua.description: Whether a Lua script is present or the table could not be inspected.

containsForms.description: Whether forms are present or the table could not be inspected.

usesMono.description: Whether the table sets UsesMono or could not be inspected.

recordCount.description: The CheatEntry count for an inspected XML table; zero for an opaque table.

assemblerScriptCount.description: The Auto Assembler script count for an inspected XML table; zero for an opaque table.

requires.description: The feature switches this particular table required and the tool enforced before loading it.

monoAutoAttach.description: Whether this load could trigger Cheat Engine's Mono data-collector auto attach.

name: table_save
title: Save cheat table
description: Save the current table through CheatEngine.Client to a .CT, .XML or .CETRAINER path under CheatEngineClient:AllowedTableRoots. overwrite must be true when a destination file already exists. A native save failure can leave a partially written destination.

path.description: The absolute destination table path inside CheatEngineClient:AllowedTableRoots.

overwrite.description: Whether an existing destination may be replaced.

path.description: The absolute table destination admitted by CheatEngine.Client's allowed table roots.

replacedExisting.description: Whether a file existed at the destination immediately before the save began.

name: util_calculate
title: Calculate a 64-bit expression
description: Evaluate an integer expression with unsigned 64-bit wraparound. Literals are decimal or 0x hexadecimal. Supported operators are + - * / % << >> & ^ | ~ and parentheses; division is unsigned and division by zero is refused.

name: util_convert_value
title: Convert a value
description: Convert a bounded value through its byte representation without accessing the target. Numeric and pointer bytes are presented in the requested byte order; UTF-8 and UTF-16 strings keep their encoding order. The source and target scalar byte counts must match.

value.description: The input value, using the same text syntax as memory_read and memory_write.

sourceType.description: The type used to parse value.

targetType.description: The type used to decode the converted bytes.

pointerSize.description: The pointer width for pointer inputs or outputs: 4 or 8.

sourceType.description: The value type used to parse the input.
